html.033: Calendar Connection and Sync Guide | Air Calendar
html.038:
From connecting a calendar
to your first sync.
html.039:
Choose the service you want to bring events from, then follow the screens below.
Connect an account → Choose calendars → Run sync → Check the result.
html.040: Connecting an external account is optional. You can use local calendars without signing in.
html.044: This diagram explains the full workflow. Click it to enlarge. CalDAV connections for Yahoo, Zoho and Fastmail are also covered below.
html.059: Click the sync icon at the top of Air Calendar.
html.060: You can also open Settings → Calendars and sync → Calendars / accounts and synchronization. The window that opens is titled Calendar management.
html.061: Click the ‘Connections and subscriptions’ tab at the top.
html.062: The window may initially show My calendars. To add an account, start in Connections and subscriptions. The Google Calendar and Subscribe by address cards appear first.
html.064: To find Outlook, iCloud, Naver, Yahoo, Zoho or Fastmail, click Show services beside Connect another account and scroll down. If you have already connected an account, the button may instead read Connection settings, Reconnect or Choose calendars to import.
html.066: Where to start: Connections and subscriptions at the top → Connect account on your service's card. Expand the service list to find additional services.
html.067: The screenshots show the matching app language with example data. Account names, calendar names and connection status vary by user. Click an image to view it at full size. In some app languages, newer controls still use English; this guide follows the labels actually shown.
html.070: ‘Two-way’ means that event changes are sent to and received from that service. It does not automatically copy Google events to Outlook. Shared calendars may be read-only, depending on the write permissions granted to your account.
html.071: Click a service name to jump to its setup steps.
html.076: Google account + Desktop app OAuth JSON file
html.079: Microsoft account + client ID for a calendar integration app
html.088: Account email + the authentication password required by the service
html.091: An iCal / ICS subscription address supplied by the service
html.093: ¹ Edit recurring and invited CalDAV events in the original service. ² Naver connections on Windows may be restricted by service policy.
html.094: Where should I enter credentials and passwords?
html.095: Use only the app's file picker and password fields described below. You do not need to enter anything on this guide page. Do not publish JSON files, app-specific passwords or private ICS addresses in posts or screenshots.
html.098: The current app connects using a Desktop app OAuth credentials file that you provide. Create the file once in Google Cloud, then sign in with the Google account you want to use in Air Calendar.
html.099: A. One-time preparation: create a Google credentials JSON file
html.100: Create a project in Google Cloud.
html.101: Sign in to Google Cloud Console. Open the project selector at the top and choose New project. Enter a name, create the project, then select it.
html.103: Open APIs & Services → Library, search for Google Calendar API and click Enable or Enable API.
html.104: Set up the consent screen in Google Auth Platform.
html.105: Open Google Auth Platform → Branding. For a new setup, click Get started and enter an app name (for example, My Air Calendar connection), a support email and a contact email. For a personal Gmail account, set the audience to External. For an internal organization account, follow your administrator's policy.
html.106: Check test users and calendar permissions.
html.107: If an external app is in testing mode, open Audience → Test users → Add users, enter the Google email you will connect and save it. Under Data Access → Add or remove scopes, select the Google Calendar API scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar and save.
html.108: Create a ‘Desktop app’ client and download its JSON file.
html.109: Click Clients → Create client. Choose Desktop app as the application type, enter a name and create the client. Download its JSON file and keep it in an easy-to-find folder on your PC. A file created for the Web application type cannot be used here.
html.110: Google's screens may vary by account and language. See Google's official desktop authentication setup guide and consent screen and test user instructions. You do not need to install Python or run the sample code for these steps.
html.111: B. Connect in Air Calendar and choose calendars to import
html.112: Click ‘Connect account’ on the Google Calendar card.
html.113: In Google settings, select Account connection. Expand OAuth file and connection help, then use Credentials file → Browse to select the OAuth JSON file you downloaded. On a PC being set up for the first time, this section may already be expanded.
html.114: Click ‘Connect Google account’ and approve access in your browser.
html.115: Choose the Google account you want to use, review the calendar access request and approve it. The app waits up to 3 minutes. Return to Air Calendar when approval is complete. Make sure the account you sign in with is also the one you added as a test user.
html.117: Click in this order: OAuth file and connection help → Browse → Connect Google account.
html.119: The app opens this screen after connecting successfully. Select only the personal, work or shared calendars you want to use. If a newly created calendar is missing, click Refresh list. Also check whether each calendar is Editable / Read-only.
html.121: Check the confirmation that settings were saved, then click Close. Save Settings does not close the window. If you close it before saving, the import choices you just made will not be applied.
html.122: Return to Calendar management and click ‘Sync now’.
html.123: You can also click Refresh on the service card to update Google alone. Finish the sync and visibility checks below to complete your first connection.
html.125: What to check: Check Import for each calendar → click Save Settings below. Check whether its events are visible afterward in My calendars.
html.126: A successful ‘Test Calendar Access’ does not mean events have finished downloading.
html.127: The access test checks permissions. After syncing, look at the calendar to confirm that events have arrived. Google automatic sync is on by default, with a regular interval of 10 minutes and a quick sync interval of 30 seconds after edits.
html.130: You can connect a personal Microsoft account or a work or school account. The current connection method requires the client ID of a Microsoft app registered for calendar integration. If your organization has provided an ID, skip the preparation and start at B.
html.131: A. If you do not have a client ID: preparation for an administrator or app registration owner
html.132: Register an app in Microsoft Entra.
html.133: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. Enter a name and select Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts as the supported account type. If you cannot register apps, ask your organization's administrator.
html.135: In the registered app, open Authentication → Add a platform → Mobile and desktop applications. Add http://localhost as a redirect URI and save.
html.137: Under API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions, check Calendars.ReadWrite and User.Read. Obtain administrator consent if your organization requires it.
html.139: Use the UUID-format ID shown on the app's Overview page in Air Calendar. A client secret is not required.
html.140: Microsoft's official app registration guide · Desktop app authentication setup
html.141: B. Sign in through the app and import events
html.142: Expand the additional service list in ‘Connections and subscriptions’.
html.143: Click Outlook · Microsoft 365 → Connect account. In the window that opens, select the 1. Connect account tab.
html.144: Expand ‘App registration and setup guide’ and enter your client ID.
html.145: Enter the Application (client) ID prepared for calendar integration. Click Sign in with Microsoft and complete sign-in and permission approval in your browser. Work or school accounts may require administrator approval or MFA.
html.147: Click in this order: 1. Connect account → enter the client ID → Sign in with Microsoft → 2. Choose calendars.
html.148: In ‘2. Choose calendars’, check the calendars to import.
html.149: Click Save calendar selection, then Sync now. If you have changed your selection but have not saved it yet, Save selection and sync lets you do both at once.
html.150: Check the result, then enable automatic sync if you want it.
html.151: Check for Sync completed and the number of imported items. To enable automatic updates, save your calendars first, then check Automatically synchronize every 5 minutes. Automatic sync is off when you first connect an account.
html.152: Outlook currently imports events from 120 days before today to 400 days ahead. Editing full recurrence rules, responding to invitations and moving connected events to another calendar are not supported. Use Outlook itself for these actions.
html.153: View the Outlook calendar selection screen
html.155: Follow Check calendars → Save calendar selection → Sync now. Choose automatic updates after saving.
html.158: A. Generate an app-specific password with Apple
html.159: Use an Apple Account with two-factor authentication enabled.
html.160: Sign in to your Apple Account.
html.161: Create a password under ‘Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords’.
html.162: Click the generate button and enter a name, such as Air Calendar. Keep the generated password ready to paste into the app. This connection uses an app-specific password instead of your usual Apple Account sign-in password.
html.163: See Apple's official app-specific password instructions. Changing or resetting your main Apple Account password revokes existing app-specific passwords, so you will need to generate a new one.
html.164: B. Enter your email and app-specific password in Air Calendar
html.165: In the additional service list, click ‘iCloud → Connect account’.
html.166: The Connect a CalDAV account window opens. Check that Calendar service at the top is set to iCloud, then select the 1. Connect account tab.
html.167: Enter your Apple email under ‘Account’ and the generated password under ‘App-specific password’.
html.168: The app sets the server address automatically. Click Verify connection and find calendars and wait for the calendar list. The password field may clear when the connection starts.
html.170: What to enter: Select iCloud at the top, enter your Apple email in Account, and enter the password generated by Apple in App-specific password.
html.171: Check calendars in ‘2. Choose calendars’, then click ‘Save selection’.
html.172: Next, click Sync now. If you have not saved yet, use Save selection and sync. Signing in and loading the calendar list alone do not finish importing events.
html.173: Check that events have arrived and choose whether to enable automatic sync.
html.174: If you want automatic updates, save your calendars, then check Automatically synchronize every 5 minutes. Personal events with write permission sync both ways. Edit recurring and invited events in the original service.
html.175: View the CalDAV calendar selection screen
html.177: Other CalDAV services use the same 2. Choose calendars tab. Check whether editing is allowed, then click Save selection.
html.181: View imported events in Air Calendar; add, edit and delete them in Naver Calendar. Naver's official instructions cover iOS and macOS, so connections from Windows may be restricted by account or server policy.
html.182: Prepare your Naver ID and authentication password.
html.183: For a personal ID with two-step verification, generate an application password in your Naver account security settings. For a personal ID without two-step verification, use your Naver sign-in password. Group IDs with two-step verification do not support application passwords and cannot connect this way.
html.184: In the additional service list, click ‘Naver → Connect account’.
html.185: Check that the service at the top of Connect a CalDAV account is Naver. In 1. Connect account, enter your Naver ID in Account and the password you prepared in Authentication password, then click Verify connection and find calendars.
html.186: Check calendars in ‘2. Choose calendars’, then save and sync.
html.187: Click Save selection → Sync now or Save selection and sync. Check the result, then enable Automatically synchronize every 5 minutes if needed.
html.188: See Naver's official CalDAV and authentication password guide. If the connection is refused, check your password, account type and the service's current support policy.
html.191: These three services use the same Connect a CalDAV account window as iCloud. Open Connections and subscriptions → Show services and click Connect account for your service, or change Calendar service at the top of the CalDAV window.
html.193: Enter your full email address in Account and a password generated by Yahoo in App-specific password. Check whether you can generate one in Yahoo's official app password help. Yahoo! JAPAN accounts are not supported.
html.195: First, choose the calendars to synchronize in Zoho Calendar under Settings → Synchronize → CalDAV. In the app, enter your full email address and authentication password, then choose the Account data center server matching your account's region. An app-specific password is required if you use two-factor authentication. See Zoho's official CalDAV guide.
html.197: In Fastmail, open Settings → Privacy & Security → Connected apps & API tokens, go to app password management and create an app password with Calendars access. Enter your full sign-up email address and this password in the app. The Basic plan does not support CalDAV or app passwords. See Fastmail's official app password guide.
html.198: Enter the service's details, then click ‘Verify connection and find calendars’.
html.199: If the connection fails, click Service authentication guide in the window to open the service's official help.
html.200: Check the calendars you want in ‘2. Choose calendars’.
html.201: Import events with Save selection → Sync now or Save selection and sync. Then enable Automatically synchronize every 5 minutes if needed.
html.202: CalDAV imports events from 120 days before today to 400 days ahead. Personal events sync both ways when you have write permission. Edit read-only calendars, recurring events and invited events in the original service. Moving connected events to a different calendar is also unsupported.
html.204: Subscribe to a calendar with an ICS address
html.205: Import read-only calendars that provide a subscription address, such as holidays, events or public schedules. No Google or Microsoft sign-in is needed.
html.206: Copy an iCal / ICS subscription address from the original service.
html.207: In your calendar service's sharing or export settings, look for a link labeled iCal, ICS or subscription address. This is different from the normal calendar webpage URL in your browser. Addresses starting with https://, http:// or webcal:// are supported.
html.208: In Calendar management, open ‘ICS subscriptions’ and click ‘Add ICS subscription’.
html.209: The Subscribe to a calendar by address window opens. Paste the link into 1. Subscription address (required), then enter a recognizable name, such as Team events, in 2. Calendar name (required).
html.210: Click ‘Add subscription’ and wait for the import result.
html.211: The button becomes available when the address format and name are valid. The address format is valid confirms the format only; it does not mean the app has connected to the server or received events. The first refresh starts after you add the subscription.
html.213: What to enter: Enter the actual ICS subscription address above and a calendar name to display in the app below. The example address cannot be used as a real subscription.
html.214: Select the subscription you added and check its ‘Last refreshed’ time.
html.215: If you see No events have been fetched yet., the first fetch has not completed. Enable Refresh this subscription and try Refresh this subscription now. Also enable Show in calendar views to display its events.
html.216: View ICS subscription visibility and refresh settings
html.218: Check Show in calendar views and Refresh this subscription separately. The sample's ‘No events have been fetched yet.’ status does not indicate a completed fetch.
html.219: If the address changes, edit the existing subscription.
html.220: Select the same subscription and use Edit subscription URL → Save changes to preserve its name, color, visibility settings and existing events. The app checks hourly while it is running, provided automatic refresh and refresh for that subscription are both enabled. Add, edit and delete the original events in the original service.
html.223: Save your calendar selection, then click ‘Sync now’.
html.224: The common button in Calendar management refreshes your connected services together. You can also check one service using its Refresh button or Sync now in that service's settings. The default shortcut is F5; use your assigned key if you have changed it.
html.225: Check both the completion status and an actual event.
html.226: Check the latest sync or refresh time and result message. Note the date and title of an event in the original service, then open the same date in Air Calendar. Signing in successfully does not mean that events have finished downloading.
html.228: Select an imported calendar and enable Show in calendar views in its details. If an event exists in the original service but is missing here, check this setting first.
html.229: Choose where new events will be saved.
html.230: To create new events in an external calendar, select Default save beside a calendar you can write to. Read-only calendars cannot be selected. You can also check the destination under Save new events to on the main calendar.
html.232: What to check: Show in calendar views controls visibility; Default save controls where new events are created.
html.233: Three settings that are easy to confuse
html.235: This chooses which calendars receive changes from the original service. Previously imported events may remain when you deselect a calendar. In Google, changes to editable events that remain can still be sent to the original service even when import is off, so deselecting is not the same as disconnecting.
html.237: This controls visibility only. Hiding a calendar keeps its sync and default save settings. You can also change visibility with the Visible button on the main screen.
html.238: Default save / Save new events to
html.239: This sets the destination for newly created events. To create events in Google Calendar, select that Google calendar rather than a local calendar.
html.240: If you create a test event, choose a calendar you can write to. Editing or deleting the event and then syncing also changes it in the original service. Rename Google calendars in Google Calendar itself.
html.243: Automatic sync runs while Air Calendar is running. First check the result of a manual sync, then choose your preferred update behavior. Connecting an account and turning automatic updates on or off are separate settings.
html.245: Open Connection settings → Sync settings → Automatically sync Google Calendar. It is on by default, with a regular interval of 10 minutes and quick sync after edits of 30 seconds. After changing an interval, click Save Settings. Manual sync remains available when automatic sync is off.
html.247: Save at least one calendar in 2. Choose calendars, then enable Automatically synchronize every 5 minutes. It is off by default for a new account. Manual Sync now is available even when automatic updates are off.
html.249: Check both automatic updates for all ICS subscriptions and Refresh this subscription for each one. The automatic interval is 1 hour. If refresh is enabled for an individual subscription, you can use Refresh this subscription now even when overall automatic refresh is off.
html.250: For a quick toggle, use Refresh automatically on the service's card in Connections and subscriptions. This switch takes effect immediately.
html.253: After changing intervals, click Save Settings at the bottom.
html.256: Open Calendar management → Troubleshoot and select the service. Depending on its status, the next action may be Reconnect, Choose calendars to import, Review pending items or Sync again.
html.259: Select the service with a problem on the left, then read the explanation and action buttons on the right.
html.260: I signed in, but there are no events
html.261: Check in this order: ① Did you select calendars to import and save? → ② Did Sync now finish? → ③ Is My calendars → Show in calendar views enabled? → ④ Are you viewing the original event's date? For Outlook and CalDAV, also check the range of 120 days back to 400 days ahead.
html.263: First finish connecting your account, select at least one calendar and save. If an operation is already running, wait for it to finish. After changing your selection, the button may become Save selection and sync.
html.265: Check that the JSON is for a Desktop app, the Calendar API is enabled and the test user email matches the account you sign in with. If approval is restricted, read the reason on Google's screen and contact the project owner or organization administrator. Use Reconnect to approve access again after expiration or permission changes.
html.266: The connection fails even with an app-specific password
html.267: Check the selected service, email or ID, and whether the app password is current and has not been revoked. Also check Apple password changes, Zoho's data center, your Fastmail plan, and Naver account or platform restrictions. Open Service authentication guide in the settings window for official help.
html.268: The ICS address is valid, but no events arrive
html.269: Format validation and fetching events are separate. Check that you entered a subscription address rather than a normal webpage URL, and that a private link has not expired. Select the existing subscription, use Edit subscription URL → Save changes, then refresh again.
html.270: An event edited on both sides has different versions
html.271: In Google settings, open Troubleshooting → Open Issues, compare the contents and choose Keep Local or Use Google Version. Google may record a conflict and apply the remote version first. For Outlook and CalDAV, open 3. Review issues in the service's settings window.
html.272: Editing or deleting an event is restricted
html.273: Edit read-only calendars and Naver or ICS events in the original service. Use the original service for recurring or invited CalDAV events, and for full Outlook recurrence rules or invitation responses.
html.274: I want to stop using a connection
html.275: To stop automatic updates, turn them off for that service. To disconnect an account, use Disconnect in its settings. For ICS, use Unsubscribe. These actions do not delete events in the original service; previously imported events may remain. To review or revoke the app's server-side access as well, check the service's account security settings.
html.277: Post the service name, the button you clicked and the error message on the user request board. Before uploading a screenshot or diagnostic report, check and hide email addresses, event details, file paths and credentials.
